checks: Since A≥0 and m>0, q=floor(A/m) and u=A−qm satisfy the stated unique division with q≥0 and 0≤u<m. The proposed finite allocation stays within every cap and has mass A. When q=0 there are no full sites; when u=0 the cutoff site has zero mass. With A=0 both allocations are identically zero.

The substitution j=h−i is bijective for every integer h. Equal total masses justify subtraction of q from the coefficient in the finite comparison. Before q the comparison value is at capacity so (j−q)(v_j−b_j)≥0; after q it is zero so the same product is nonnegative; at q the coefficient vanishes. This proves the distance-moment minimum, attained by the displayed allocation.

Independently expanding A=qm+u gives A²−mA+u(m−u)=m²q(q−1)+2mqu. Thus the claimed correction to the upper bound on the first moment has the minus sign. Converting back gives hA minus the distance moment. Independently enumerated 234 mass/capacity/support-size combinations for integer mass units (caps 1–4, consecutive supports of size 1–6), including fractional multiples of a full cap and exact multiples; the sharp values and the cleared-denominator identity matched.

Verified both cited source byte hashes against base 27bf01c and checked locators: 3c669076dab13e6a §1 (6) gives the one-sided packing bound with its remainder; ad8324f468564d7c §3 (4) explicitly records the filled-site value and remainder. The frozen proof directly supplies the cutoff comparison behind those source arguments.

overlap.comparison: This fixed-mass, fixed-first-moment result gives linear cost optimality under finite site capacities. It treats the first moment as a constraint, so it does not supply the largest feasible first moment for a prescribed mass or its exact integer remainder.

The continuous bathtub calculation maximizes a directional moment under a density cap. Filling whole unit intervals can recover the weaker quadratic bound from its continuous counterpart, but the continuous formula has no discrete fractional remainder.
Its continuous interval first-moment calculation likewise has no uniform integer site constraint and no exact discrete remainder.
Pending source §3 already contains the same exact scalar extremum within a separate d=1 tail argument; it is not an accepted fact.
Pending source §1 includes the same packing calculation inside an all-degree tail argument; it is not an accepted fact.
